_about: F39 RANK TWISTS (GDD rank twists; v1 numbers from research/v1/PRD.md): from rank 20 some pieces fall in two colours (two even, connected halves that lock as two clumps); from rank 30 cracks grow into the cells next to them (a grown crack is ONE crack: sealed only when every cell is covered by its colour, then it counts its cell count toward the quota; it drains per cell); from rank 40 some pieces are wild goop (plugs any crack colour; a normal piece landing next to a wild clump turns the whole clump its colour). Read by the engine (src/engine/twists.ts) at the moment each number is used, on the rules clock — live in the Dev Kit. Seeded by the shift's random numbers, so ?seed plays repeat. Chances are 0..1, times in ms.

_help.split.fromRank: Two-colour pieces start at this rank.
_help.split.chance: The share of pieces that fall in two colours (0.25 = one in four). Corrupt and wild pieces never split.
_help.grow.fromRank: Cracks start growing at this rank.
_help.grow.everyMsMin: Each uncovered crack cell rolls to grow once every so often: at least this long between rolls…
_help.grow.everyMsMax: …and at most this long (picked at random in between each time). Slow Cracks stretches it.
_help.grow.baseChance: The chance a roll grows the crack, before pressure (0.1 = 10%).
_help.grow.pressureWeight: How much pressure adds to that chance: chance = base + pressure × this (v1: 1, so 10% at empty → 110% at full).
_help.grow.leafMult: A cell with nothing grown from it yet is this much less likely to grow (v1: 0.5) — so cracks branch rather than snake.
_help.grow.hopFalloff: Each step a cell is from where the crack formed takes this off its chance (v1: 0.25 a step)…
_help.grow.minFalloff: …but never below this share of it (v1: 0.1).
_help.grow.diagonals: true = a crack can grow into the 8 cells round it (v1); false = only up, down, left, right.
_help.wild.fromRank: Wild goop starts at this rank.
_help.wild.chance: The share of pieces that are wild goop (0.15 = about one in seven). Corrupt pieces are never wild; wild is never two-colour.
